Executive summary

Study status: PARTIAL. The public-method inventory spans all seven NUMERIX modules, but Phase 14B measurements currently cover root finding only. This dashboard shows measured root results and explicitly marks all remaining module methods as pending.
49NUMERIX public methods / operations audited
7numerical modules in the API
8candidate libraries listed
3libraries measured for root methods
100frozen root problems per method route
1,700root accuracy records
52,700raw root timing batches
322root edge-case outcomes

Root routes measured: NUMERIX 9, GSL 7, CMINPACK 1. Each root route includes 100 frozen problems; timing uses 31 independent batches per problem and method, with two warmups. Edge suite: 19 cases, 21 timing batches per measured case/library-method pair. Root adapters use a common 500-iteration cap; work counters are collected only in untimed accuracy probes.

Measured direct root comparisons

The paired unit is the problem. A pair is included only when both libraries are applicable, successful, and accurate. The confidence intervals below are descriptive problem-level bootstrap intervals; no statistical significance or overall library winner is claimed.

MethodEligible pairsExcludedGSL / NUMERIX median time95% bootstrap interval

secant85151.08[1.06, 1.09]

brent9551.04[1.02, 1.06]

Direct comparison summary: bisection: ratio 1.08, 95% CI [1.07, 1.1], n=94; regula_falsi: ratio 1.02, 95% CI [0.987, 1.04], n=95; secant: ratio 1.08, 95% CI [1.06, 1.09], n=85; newton: ratio 1.07, 95% CI [1.06, 1.08], n=90; brent: ratio 1.04, 95% CI [1.02, 1.06], n=95

Multiple-root discovery is a best-available heuristic comparison. NUMERIX detected 100/100 expected roots in this frozen set; GSL’s fixed 4096-panel sign-change scan detected 94/100 and missed six. The GSL scan has no tangential-root guarantee. NUMERIX’s discovery API reports unresolved intervals and multiplicity estimates; GSL’s scan reports unresolved regions as unavailable.

Memory analysis

No method-specific allocation interception was completed in Phase 14B. Existing Phase 14 RSS includes the harness and process baseline, so it is not used here as a per-method library memory comparison. Requested heap bytes, allocator metadata, stack, and shared dependency allocations are unavailable. No memory winner is reported.

Method coverage and API boundary

The verified initial inventory contains 49 public methods and operations: root 9, linear algebra 20, differentiation 7, interpolation 4, integration 4, optimization 2, and ODE 3. Method coverage includes public numerical algorithms, linear-algebra primitives, lifecycle calls requested by the benchmark brief, piecewise adapters, and root orchestration/discovery. Supporting expression, diagnostic, and managed-execution utilities are documented as API boundaries, not silently counted as standalone numerical methods.

Methodology and statistical interpretation

  • Frozen Phase 14 problem IDs were reused. Root comparisons used identical function definitions, brackets/starts, tolerances, and references; eligibility was separately recorded.
  • 31 timing batches per normal root problem-method-library route; two warmups. Direct iterative calls used four repetitions per batch, orchestration two, and root-discovery one. Edge cases use 21 batches and one repetition.
  • Work counters are collected in a separate untimed probe. Wall and process CPU time are retained. Per-problem medians, not the 31 repeated batches, are the unit for paired comparisons and bootstrap confidence intervals.
  • Paired direct ratios require both applicable, successful, accuracy-passing outputs and positive measured times. Exclusions remain in the raw accuracy records. The ratio is median GSL time divided by median NUMERIX time.
  • Holm correction was considered. No hypothesis tests or familywise significance claims are made; intervals are descriptive and therefore are not adjusted.
  • Method call timing includes library solver/workspace calls and excludes input parsing, process launch, and CSV writing. Setup and conversion are not separately measured for all routes.

Limitations and outstanding scope

  • Only root finding has Phase 14B method-level raw measurements and edge runs. Six modules remain unmeasured.
  • Time-to-accuracy tolerance sweeps were not run; one configured tolerance per problem was checked.
  • Method-specific allocation instrumentation and memory comparisons are not available.
  • Root discovery is heuristic; NUMERIX reports unresolved regions while the GSL scan cannot provide equivalent unresolved-region or multiplicity metrics.
  • CMINPACK is a best-available one-variable hybrid-system comparison, not direct Newton equivalence. GSL’s safeguarded-Newton route uses Brent and is best-available.
  • The GSL discovery baseline scans 4096 subintervals and refines sign changes, so it can miss tangential roots.
  • The Phase 14B CMake file is provided, but CMake was unavailable in this shell. The adapter was compiled with the recorded GCC command and linked against locally built pinned dependencies. This remains a build reproducibility limitation.
